comments.body: btw, i cann share some feedback already, your temperature is too high, models are getting lost easy, you are chaining next step from previews one which together with high temp leads to looping, agent is getting stuck doing same thing over and over over-consuming the api, you should implement supervising model to orchestrate rather than chined. Thats all for now, cant test anymore due to rate limit kicking me off and i dont have time to wait until it goes off, good luck! i like what i see thus far and love the direction

Sorry for the rate limit. You can see https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-copilot-release/issues/4493. The looping issue you're describing is likely https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-copilot-release/issues/5550. You can try downgrading the extension a version (right click on the extension > install specific version) to get rid of that bug.

Also the temperature is already very low, even if it doesn't seem like it 😅 and we are working on other agent strategies and prompt improvements.

Can I help in any way? Is the plugin code public? I’m fairly sure if my
feedback is actioned a lot of the loops can be avoided. Model that
specifically ends in loops is the sonet, shame as it’s best coding model.
Again I’m happy to contribute and help any way I can.

Additionally, quite often i end up having this error: Sorry, your request failed. Please try again. Request id: fc585a26-e4a4-43f3-ae36-893c7878499a

Reason: Request Failed: 400 Bad Request
No amount of refresh helps, i think the payload is not escaped (sanitized) correctly causing the 400 bad request, again without seeing the plugin code its hard to speculate but this error happens quite often. 

UPDATE: problem only went away when i shut down vsc and restarted agent session, couldnt get out of the 400 in any other way
I'm getting continuous 400 errors as well, using edits on VSCode Stable.

small update, thanks for the new models, especially the new sonnet, it is actually very good. I wanted to share some feedback on the only non-preview 4o, it sucks really bad now. Yes before was very hot-headed, jumping too quickly and even breaking what it wrote previously, all this considered it actually did something, it was super junior level but actually writing code, now, it is like an old mule, I have spent 10min talking to it that it did not do the job it said it did but every time it told me the job is done, it confirmed and everything is done when nothing was. So 4o is now close to unusable, thankfully 3.7 is saving the day thus far, will test more and will try to share more feedback. Again good job guys, keep it coming!

Several updates later, this crazy rate limit is still kicking in after barely a few prompts and once in, turns the copilot completely useless for the day as once you rate limited it gives you a warning to wait a few minutes after those few minutes the window tightens and the limit is applied every second request rendering this agent mode practically unusable as waiting time is in hours to return to a usable state. Hunch tells me that it could be due to the fact that the longer you work, more files the agent accumulates in its context and it uses them all on every request which leads to a very large context and large token consumtion

Guys, i have got no response on ask for lifting the cooldown/rate limit. If this is not addressed I will be moving from copilot altogether, there are better tools lie cursor or windsurf these days that do not impose those limits you do. Please address my concern

The rate limit for 4o and Claude 3.5 is fairly high, although you can certainly hit it with intense usage. For 3.7 I believe it's lower, so you may be able to try a different model to continue. This is just a rate limit on response tokens, not input tokens.

We've made some improvements- when agent mode hit the rate limit, it would hide the response content from previous tool calls in the same turn. That's fixed at least. Also, it was giving a time estimate, which is valid for chat, but not actually helpful in agent mode where we generally need to make multiple requests in order to do anything. We can't get a better time estimate right now, so I just hid the time limit.

Sorry, I know that the rate limit is annoying, especially in agent mode. We can't increase it right now but we will keep looking into it! You can see https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/troubleshooting-github-copilot/troubleshooting-common-issues-with-github-copilot#error-sorry-your-request-was-rate-limited for more details (this is written more about Chat, I understand that it's much easier to hit in agent mode)

As much as I want to be loyal and cheer you to the end of the world Rob, the reality is reality and it doesn't favour you and trust me, my experience is everyone's experience. It is 11:53 am when I'm writing this, I have been working on a simple .net API project switching between models but mostly working on what you mentioned 3.5 sonnet as it has better limits. 3 hours into my day I got this: "Sorry, you have exhausted this model's rate limit. Please wait a moment before trying again, or switch to a different model." 3h, it doesn't matter how you sugarcoat it or justify, your tool is no longer usable and you are badly losing to your competitors. Please review your limits or this is the last time you hear from one of your most loyal client (with you since day 1)

I agree that agent mode is frustrating with rate-limits, and only being able to use 4o is not as good as the other options.
A fix could be to allow for third parties implementations or to allow for local LLM connectivities like Cline.
or even to have the ability to insert personal api keys to connect to the model when we've reached the limit-rate. Which I assume are due to the princing or the infrastructure requirements or licensing.
Anyways, still very fustrating to have an agent that can't run to the fullest of its ability.

I tried my best, and raised the fact that I was frustrated and disappointed with the fact that I paid the license in full, yet, that locked me out of the entire copilot. Cursor for example will never lock you out and will at a fixed fee will let you work as long as you want, they downgrade the model but they will not lock you from the tools you use. I did try, I am one of the first adopters of Copilot and was a user all the way from the beta phase, but if I cannot use the tool and only pay for it, you get to wonder who is working for whom here. I am sorry to say that I am cancelling my subscription and moving with a competitor, they have this already solved. Here no one even replied to my original request for over 2 weeks now. Very disappointed ex-customer, one who will not be recommending the service anytime soon.
@roblourens Any ETA for solution? or in march 2025 vs code and copilot update?

Hitting exactly the same issue..   Being rate limited within 1-2 hours of a development day and then have completely stop loosing all context.  And I'm not just talking the 'Preview' models.   GPT-4o as well, the supposed 'standard model'.   What's worse is it can token fail mid way through a batch of related edits leaving your code in a state where it no longer works.

CoPilot might be cheaper than Cursor or Windsurf, but if it fails within a fraction of working day, then it really is false economy.

I gave up and cancelled my subscription.
I’m currently using my free trial of the pro version and also hitting rate limits after a few hours. Not even a third of a day. This is totally not enough for me to pay for this.
Should be working better these days

> Should be working better these days

Haha, lol, no. Can't get much done with this tool. What exactly am I paying for?

Still hitting this. Built an extension to deal with it — it watches for rate-limit and failure errors in Copilot Chat and automatically sends a follow-up message asking the agent to retry, so you don't have to sit there clicking "Try Again" or waste time when you step away.

[Copilot Auto Retry](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=MaximMazurok.vscode-copilot-auto-retry) — open-source, configurable delays/max retries, and has guardrails to avoid infinite loops.

Doesn't fix the underlying rate limits obviously, but at least the agent picks back up on its own instead of sitting dead until you notice.
